trust_decision.summary: Not an authorization decision but a resource-ownership invariant: once DBD::File::DataSource::File::open_data has flock()ed the table's .lck handle into $meta->{lockfh}, every later failure inside the table constructor must release it, because DBI::DBD::SqlEngine::Table::new calls open_data before the object is blessed (so DESTROY never runs) and $meta persists in $dbh->{sql_meta}; DBD::DBM::Table::open_data croaked after the lock with no release.

landing_point.why: The summary names DBD::DBM open_data and the ChangeLog wording ('bad serializer class') points straight at the dbm_mldbm _CLASS croak that sits after SUPER::open_data.

fix_sites.entry_point: $dbh->do / execute of CREATE, SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on a DBD::DBM table with dbm_mldbm set (DBI::SQL::Nano open_tables -> SqlEngine open_table -> Table::new -> open_data)
fix_sites.module_kind: driver table class (DBD::DBM::Table), the reported module

fix_sites.entry_point: same SQL statements; old post-lock serializer check removed
same SQL statements when tie() fails or the data file is missing after tie
SQL DROP via DBI::SQL::Nano DROP -> $table->drop; helper _release_lock extracted from drop
table object destruction after any statement

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The File.pm hunks (fix.diff:184-222) only extract the existing drop/DESTROY close+unlock code into _release_lock; no behaviour changes there, so the substantive fix is confined to DBD::DBM::Table::open_data.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and ChangeLog talk only about the 'bad serializer class' and tie failures, so a solver can argue that later croaks (metadata read/write, BerkeleyDB flag handling, the Nano col_names check in a different package) are unrelated input-validation errors, not the reported lock leak.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: DROP TABLE of a table whose dbm_mldbm is invalid must still work (fix skips the new validation in dropMode); validating in init_table_meta or unconditionally in open_data would make the bad table undroppable. Also the .lck file must survive a failed open: unlinking it (tempting given the ChangeLog's 'lock file not removed') makes every later open croak 'Cannot open ... .lck'. Shared SELECT locks must stay held for the life of a successfully opened table.

O6_input_shapes: dbm_mldbm that fails the module-name grammar (path-shaped or traversal)
tie() failure for the configured dbm_type/MLDBM combination
tie succeeds but data file absent (-f fails)
createMode, lockMode (exclusive) and read (shared) lock modes all reach the same failure points

O7_producer.where: Lock state is produced by lib/DBD/File.pm:739-768 (data-source layer, called via lib/DBI/DBD/SqlEngine.pm:1622) and persisted through $dbh->{sql_meta} at lib/DBI/DBD/SqlEngine.pm:1556-1561; this is a handler-style producer, not a schema/serializer, and the DBM code calls it directly.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Post-tie metadata block reads _metadata through the tied (possibly MLDBM-thawing) hash and writes it back even on a read-only (SELECT) tie; any die there leaves the lock held.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is past the code the advisory names and looks like data-format handling, not open/lock handling; writing metadata in SELECT is documented legitimate behaviour (lib/DBD/DBM.pm:1202-1206).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function, ~20 lines below the fixed hunk

O8_uncovered_routes.route: BerkeleyDB branch dereferences dbm_berkeley_flags as a hash after the lock is taken; a non-hash value dies with the lock held.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Needs the optional BerkeleyDB backend; a solver can call it an unsupported combination / user error.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function, above the fixed hunk

O8_uncovered_routes.route: After open_data returns, SqlEngine Table::new passes $meta->{col_names} to DBI::SQL::Nano::Table_::new, which croaks unless it is an ARRAY; in createMode DBM does not normalize a string dbm_cols ('foo,bar', documented) before this, so the croak happens unblessed with the lock held.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is in the generic SqlEngine/Nano layer, two packages from DBD::DBM, and only with Nano (no SQL::Statement); looks like an unrelated column-spec validation.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 2 files / 2 packages from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A generic post-open_data hook (e.g. column-map or encoding setup) in Table::new that can croak before bless.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The comment at lib/DBI/DBD/SqlEngine.pm:1643-1644 already says setup is done before inherited new; adding more pre-bless work there is the natural place a maintainer would extend.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Reorder so the data/lock flock happens before apply_encoding, making an encoding croak leak the lock in the base DBD::File data source (second implementation used by DBD::CSV-style drivers).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Both Stream and File data sources do open/encode/lock in slightly different orders (lib/DBD/File.pm:539-555 vs 732-768); a refactor unifying them could plausibly move the lock earlier.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Schema/col_names validation from stored _metadata (e.g. croak on column-count mismatch) after the lock.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: push_names already enforces column rules (lib/DBD/DBM.pm:536-539); mirroring them on reopen is an obvious maintainer addition.

O9_family: Improper locking / resource release on error path (CWE-667): lock leaked when constructor fails before the owning object exists

O10_build.toolchain: perl, ExtUtils::MakeMaker, C compiler for DBI.xs; DBD::DBM/DBD::File are pure Perl using core SDBM_File and Fcntl
O10_build.project_tests: t/49dbd_file.t, t/50dbm_simple.t, t/51dbm_file.t, t/52dbm_complex.t, t/53dbm_module_name.t (MLDBM case skipped unless MLDBM installed)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Move the dbm_mldbm _CLASS check above SUPER::open_data (or into init_table_meta) and stop, or unlink the .lck file on failure, instead of releasing the lock on every post-lock failure (ideally with an eval around open_data in SqlEngine Table::new).

out_of_scope_notes: lib/DBD/File.pm:730 and 748: if the lock-file open fails, the already opened data handle stays in $meta->{fh} (open handle leak, not a lock).
lib/DBD/DBM.pm:391-392 deletes DB_CREATE/DB_RDONLY from the shared dbm_berkeley_flags hash on each open (attribute mutation).
